messages.content:
This function is supposed to append a new note to a user's list of notes, creating a fresh list if none was provided.

```python
def add_note(note, notes=[]):
    if notes is None:
        notes = []
    notes.append(note)
    return notes
```

issues.input: Calling add_note(note) without providing notes, after any previous call has already appended to the default list.
issues.code_does: All calls that omit notes share and mutate the same default list created at function-definition time, so the returned 'fresh' list includes notes appended by previous unrelated calls.
issues.should_do: Each call that omits notes should receive a new, independent list containing only the note(s) added by that call.
issues.justification: The description says it should append to a user's list of notes, creating a fresh list if none was provided. Using a mutable default argument as the implicit storage means a fresh list is not created per call; it reuses the same list, so previously appended notes persist across calls. A typical reviewer would flag this as incorrect behavior.
